sections.overview: Porcellio monticola is recorded in western Europe. Spanish surveys report it from multiple Iberian provinces.
sections.identification: It is relatively large, flattened and rather smooth; it can be confused with P. montanus.
sections.habitat: It is often found beneath bark in woodland, and also in river valleys, limestone cliffs and cave entrances.
sections.diet: The accounts reviewed do not describe its diet in detail.
sections.behavior: The French account reports it throughout the year and notes that it shelters in crevices by day.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific reproductive information was not available in the accounts reviewed.
sections.ecology: A 2026 Ligurian review cautions that older records labelled P. monticola may be other species; it discusses P. spinipennis separately.
sections.conservation: No global conservation assessment was found in the sources consulted.
